reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

votes.question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendments — An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes (H R 5334)
votes.plain_language: The House voted to accept the Senate's rewrite of H.R. 5334, which imposes Russia-related sanctions and tariffs, extends an Iran sanctions law, and also expands a teacher tax deduction to early-childhood educators. A Yea accepts that Senate version. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 93)
votes.plain_language: This resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress authorizes it, except for forces needed to defend against an imminent attack if the President follows the War Powers Resolution's time limits. A Yea agrees. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Whistleblower Protection Act (H R 4646)
votes.plain_language: This bill extends whistleblower protections to employees of Housing and Urban Development contractors and grantees, including on contracts signed before 2013. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Table — Impeaching Donald John Trump, President of the United States, for high crimes and misdemeanors (H RES 1486)
votes.plain_language: The resolution would impeach President Trump over Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection practices that it says violate the Constitution. This vote was a motion to table, which kills the resolution. A Yea tables it; a Nay would have left it pending.

lobbying.bill_title: Impeaching Donald John Trump, President of the United States, for high crimes and misdemeanors.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Local Communities & Bird Habitat Stewardship Act (H R 3276)
votes.plain_language: This bill writes into law the Urban Bird Treaty program, including grants to help cities conserve birds. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

lobbying.bill_title: Local Communities & Bird Habitat Stewardship Act

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States to require that the Supreme Court of the United States be composed of nine justices (H J RES 1)
votes.plain_language: This resolution proposes a constitutional amendment fixing the Supreme Court at nine justices. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports that amendment; a Nay opposes it.

lobbying.bill_title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States to require that the Supreme Court of the United States be composed of nine justices

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — In the matter of allegations relating to Representative Chuck Edwards (H RES 1498)
votes.plain_language: This resolution censures Representative Chuck Edwards of North Carolina. A Yea votes to censure him. A Nay votes not to.

lobbying.bill_title: In the matter of allegations relating to Representative Chuck Edwards.

votes.question: On Passage — To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective (H R 9436)
votes.plain_language: This bill moves the deadline for new lobster- and crab-gear rules meant to protect North Atlantic right whales from 2028 to 2035. A Yea passes it. A Nay votes no.

lobbying.bill_title: To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective (H R 9436)
votes.plain_language: H.R. 9436 would move the deadline for new lobster- and crab-gear rules meant to protect North Atlantic right whales from 2028 to 2035. This vote would have delayed that bill until the Commerce Secretary published a report on how trade fights with Canada and China, and the war in Iran, affect fishing costs and seafood prices. A Yea would have added that delay; a Nay rejected it.

lobbying.bill_title: To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Providing for the condemnation and denouncement of socialism in all its forms, and for other purposes (H RES 1490)
votes.plain_language: This resolution condemns socialism, including the Democratic Socialists of America, and says the House supports the SAVE America Act and elections limited to U.S. citizens. A Yea agrees. A Nay does not.

lobbying.bill_title: Providing for the condemnation and denouncement of socialism in all its forms, and for other purposes.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Local Access to Courts Act (S 32)
votes.plain_language: This bill adds College Station, Texas, and El Centro, California, as places where specified federal courts must sit. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 89)
votes.plain_language: This resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress has declared war or authorized that force, while still allowing defense against an imminent attack. A Yea agrees to that direction. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran

donor_industry.caption: From itemized individual contributions over $200 reported to the FEC, grouped by the donor's self-reported employer and occupation. Employer means where the donor works, not that the company gave money; corporations can't give directly to campaigns. Industry groups use simple keyword rules and may misclassify some donors.

stands_for.caption: Grouped by Congress.gov's official policy area. Shows how they voted, not why. Final-passage, amendment, and procedural votes can mean different things; read the note for each.
stands_for.scope: House roll calls 1–323 of 2026 (323 votes, January 6, 2026 to November 12, 2026), from the House Clerk.
stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Concur in the Senate Amendments — AGOA Extension Act (H R 6500)
votes.bill_title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
votes.plain_language: The House voted to accept the Senate's rewrite of this bill, which became a stopgap that funds federal agencies into fiscal year 2027, generally through December 11, 2026, and extends several expiring programs. It is not a vote on the bill's original Africa-trade text. A two-thirds Yea accepts the Senate version; a Nay rejects it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Establishing the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2027 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2028 through 2036 (H CON RES 113)
votes.bill_title: Establishing the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2027 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2028 through 2036.
votes.plain_language: This resolution sets federal budget targets for fiscal year 2027 through 2036 and instructs several House committees to write bills that would raise the deficit by limited amounts, which can move under faster reconciliation rules. A Yea adopts that budget plan. A Nay rejects it.

votes.bill_title: Continuing Appropriations Act, 2027
votes.plain_language: This bill provides continuing FY2027 appropriations for federal agencies and extends various expiring programs and authorities. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.plain_language: This bill provides FY2027 appropriations for national security, the Department of State, and related programs. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7148)
votes.bill_title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7148 (Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to prohibit the use of funds to implement section 24220 of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, including any requirements enabling or supporting vehicle "kill switch" technology, and to prohibit federal spending for the execution or enforcement of such authorities.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Making further consolidated appropriations for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026, and for other purposes (H R 7147)
votes.bill_title: Homeland Security and Further Additional Continuing Appropriations Act, 2026.
votes.plain_language: This bill provides continuing FY2026 appropriations to the Department of Homeland Security through May 22, 2026. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Financial Services and General Government and National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 7006)
votes.bill_title: Financial Services and General Government and National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill provides FY2026 appropriations to several federal departments and agencies for activities and programs related to financial services, general government, national security, the administration of foreign affairs, and foreign assistance. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7006)
votes.bill_title: Financial Services and General Government and National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7006 is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to eliminate funding for the National Endowment for Democracy.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7006)
votes.bill_title: Financial Services and General Government and National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7006 is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to reduce the District of Columbia District and Appeals Court funding by 20% and to strike the salary and expense funding for Judges Boasberg's and Judge Boardman's staffs.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — AGOA Extension Act (H R 6500)
votes.bill_title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
votes.plain_language: This bill provides continuing FY2027 appropriations for federal agencies and extends various expiring programs and authorities. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 6938)
votes.bill_title: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill provides FY2026 appropriations to several federal departments and agencies for activities and programs related to commerce, law enforcement, science, energy and water development, public lands, and the environment. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Retaining Divisions B and C — Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 6938)
votes.bill_title: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: H.R. 6938 combines three FY2026 spending bills: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment. The House voted separately on whether to keep parts of the bill. This vote was on keeping Divisions B and C. A Yea keeps them in the bill; a Nay would remove them.

votes.question: On Retaining Division A — Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 6938)
votes.bill_title: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: H.R. 6938 combines three FY2026 spending bills: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment. The House voted separately on whether to keep parts of the bill. This vote was on keeping Division A. A Yea keeps it in the bill; a Nay would remove it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Emergency Conservation Program Improvement Act (S 629)
votes.bill_title: Emergency Conservation Program Improvement Act of 2025
votes.plain_language: This bill revises the Emergency Conservation Program and the Emergency Forest Restoration Program to expand eligibility for payments to agricultural producers and owners of forest land impacted by natural disasters. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Farm, Food, and National Security Act (H R 7567)
votes.bill_title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill reauthorizes through FY2031 and modifies Department of Agriculture programs (the farm bill), including commodity support, conservation, nutrition assistance, farm credit, rural development, forestry, and crop insurance. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Farm, Food, and National Security Act (H R 7567)
votes.bill_title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) reauthorizes through FY2031 and modifies Department of Agriculture programs (the farm bill), including commodity support, conservation, nutrition assistance, farm credit, rural development, forestry, and crop insurance. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
votes.bill_title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment removes certain emissions standards on farm equipment.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
votes.bill_title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to add "soda" to the definition of ineligible items and defines soda as a carbonated beverage containing more than 1 gram of added sugar, artificial sweetener, or flavoring per serving.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment, as Modified (H R 7567)
votes.bill_title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment revises the Agriculture Advanced Research and Development Authority program to provide federal support for sustainable agriculture and innovative sustainability solutions.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
votes.bill_title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to preserve greyhound racing operations in West Virginia.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
votes.bill_title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment strikes several sections relating to pesticide labeling requirements.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
votes.bill_title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to repeal and prohibit future implementation of the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) rule mandating electronic identification (EID) eartags for bison and cattle moving interstate.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
votes.bill_title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “An amendment numbered 20 printed in Part B of House Report 119-628 to mandate a USDA report to Congress (after the SNAP restrictions pilots are completed) on implementation of the restrictions, outcomes, recommendations to Congress.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
votes.bill_title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment adds hot rotisserie chicken as an eligible item to be purchased by SNAP benefits.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
votes.bill_title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to modify the Renewable Fuel Standard's definition of "renewable biomass".” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
vote_scope: This is not a full career record. The cache is the latest 40 House rolls (2026, rolls 275-314) and 40 Senate votes (119th Congress, session 2, votes 217-256).
